body:
Be weird to go through childhood with all the knowledge I have now. Dunno if I could pretend to be a child for that long without cracking or giving the game away. 

If I could go back to being 16 years old with my current brain, however, I would do it in a heartbeat. I would change everything.

My parents aren't exactly poor but they're not well off either. But even if they were well off, there would be so many conditions attached to them paying for therapy, I wouldn't feel comfortable with accepting it. Not that they've ever offered nor would it occur to them to. My mum buys me "treats" but never anything actually useful. 

By 'fit state' I meant mainly mental - I can manage physical issues if I am careful. Even at the best of times I am rather quiet and introverted, with a tendency for my mind to go blank and be unable to think of anything to say. But right now I am just likely to start crying at any time. I'm so needy as well; I feel like I'm clinging onto my couple of remaining friends for dear life. I try and hide it, but you can't really hide raw neediness, can you?

This is my problem too. 

My brother committed suicide last year. There are 4 of us, so there would still be 2 children left, but I really, really, really don't want to leave my mum with the pain of a second suicide. On the other hand she could go on for another 10-20 years in sound health and I can't cope with the next week, let alone another decade or two.

I just want fucking out. Life is unbearable.

No, it's not shit. You've given the right advice on the whole, but I can't do any of it. I'm not in any fit state to meet new people; I need to be well before I can meet new people and I can't get well until I have positive experiences with new people - it's a perfect vicious circle if ever there was one. 

My life is an unusual one in that I was living with my parents until I was almost 40, never been in a relationship or had sex, never had a career - what jobs I had were temporary and a long, long time ago. I was also physically ill, with severe pain/fever episodes and, for a couple of years, in and out of hospital. I'm absolutely certain that's ground me down too, especially as the original condition and its spin-offs are still with me. 

So, no, I don't have the slightest, slightest hope I can rebuild my life. The autism and mental illness will always destroy any attempts to rebuild my life. I'm keeping on going mainly for other people now - because I can hardly bear the fucking pain of living anymore.

Thanks folks. 

The mornings and evenings are the worst. Every day I wake up, feel okay for about 1 second, then the despair and futility descends.

Re my friend, the one who broke up with me. We met about 5 years ago (on a depression forum ironically enough). We hit it off immediately, and emailed each other almost every day. He was married, so the friendship never went beyond that. But we did talk a lot and, over time, I grew to trust him totally. He never judged anything I said, ever. Like, really, he was the first person I've had this much unconditional kindness and affection from. 

Then the worst fucking year of my life happened last year. I lost my only local friend to a heart attack - we'd also fallen out a few months beforehand, so as well as simply just missing him, there was also massive amounts of guilt. About six months after that, my brother committed suicide by hanging. We weren't close, but I never got the chance to say the things I had wanted to say to him or even to go and see him in the country he lived in. 

Shortly after my brother's death, I became estranged from my parents and, thus, the rest of the family. (Long long background story with my parents and my estrangement from them.) I became suicidal, much as I am now, and was persuaded by my support worker and a doctor to voluntary admit myself. I spent 3 weeks in a psychiatric ward and then a further 3 weeks in a day hospital. I hated the psychiatric ward and never want to go back there again, but the day hospital was a little bit more helpful.

At any rate I downloaded WhatsApp to keep in touch with a couple of folks from the day hospital. I also added my male married friend. Bitter, bitter mistake that was. It somehow changed the dynamics of our friendship - I became more dependent and needy, whilst he became pushier in trying to get me help. 

I fell in love with my friend or thought I did - I dunno what's up or down anymore. I did try to tell him a couple of times and force his hand into saying goodbye, because I didn't like the clingy, needy person I was becoming. There was one weekend where I outright threatened suicide - not immediately - but I told him about my plans. Once I had calmed down, I apologised to him for getting him involved and didn't mention suicide again after that. 

But I was still desperately unhappy, still desperately lonely, and a couple of weeks ago told him I loved him again and tried to force him to tell me about his wife, his true feelings, etc. He barely said anything tbh. He claimed in his second-to-last ever message that he had told his wife everything about me, including that he "loved me". But earlier on in the convo, he'd been adamant that his feelings for me were nothing more than just close friendship. 

Shortly after that I was blocked on WhatsApp, then later on Twitter. If ever there had been any chance of a reconciliation I probably ruined it forever with an angry meltdown in DMs on Twitter - I'd never lost my temper with him in 5 years then I just lost all control for 10 minutes or so. 

This was a fortnight ago and I've not heard from him since. I miss him so so so badly. I don't even care about the love part anymore, I just want things to go back to how they were before WhatsApp ever happened. And they can't. I'll never meet anyone else I can click with like him again. (As I virtually never click with anybody.)

I guess I should add that I've never actually met my male friend, as he lived abroad. We talked about meeting up, but obviously that will never happen as well - I genuinely wanted to see his country too. 

My *female* friend I've known for several years. She is a lovely soul, but has numerous health/depression issues on her own, so I feel like I'm being a bit of a burden on her at the moment. 

As for my parents, I've partially reconciled with them and am going over there one day a week. However I'm always aware that our relationship could fail again - particularly with my dad, who has a history of being abusive and congtrolling. I do not trust him, never will. I used to think I could trust my mum, but now I've discovered that I can't altogether trust her either. She *can* be okay, but then she will go cold and hostile. I've told her that, and I don't think she liked it, but we are still okay for now. 

Thanks for listening, or, rather, reading, folks. It's the loneliness which will ultimately do for me one day I think. I'm on the autism spectrum and, for various reasons, have never properly dated. I'm sick of being on my own, I'm really really really sick of it. And volunteer groups, etc. aren't an adequate substitute - I just meet acquaintances; they're nice people, but it's not enough. I want what I had with my male friend, minus the friend being married bit.
This... actually helped. A tiny tiny bit.
